**Problem.** Evaluate
$$L=\lim_{n\to\infty}\sqrt{n}\int_{-1/\sqrt{n}}^{0} e^{x^{2}/2}\,\operatorname{erfi}\!\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2n}}\right)dx.$$

**Key observation.** The factor $\operatorname{erfi}\!\bigl(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2n}}\bigr)$ is constant in $x$, so it factors out of the integral:
$$L_n:=\sqrt{n}\,\operatorname{erfi}\!\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2n}}\right)\int_{-1/\sqrt{n}}^{0} e^{x^{2}/2}\,dx.$$

**Asymptotics of the erfi factor.** For small $z$,
$$\operatorname{erfi}(z)=\frac{2}{\sqrt{\pi}}\left(z+\frac{z^{3}}{3}+O(z^{5})\right).$$
With $z=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2n}}\to 0$,
$$\operatorname{erfi}\!\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2n}}\right)=\frac{2}{\sqrt{\pi}}\cdot\frac{1}{\sqrt{2n}}\left(1+\frac{1}{6n}+O(n^{-2})\right)=\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}}\,\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\left(1+O(n^{-1})\right).$$

**Asymptotics of the integral.** Since $e^{x^{2}/2}=1+\frac{x^{2}}{2}+O(x^{4})$ near $x=0$,
$$\int_{-1/\sqrt{n}}^{0} e^{x^{2}/2}\,dx=\int_{-1/\sqrt{n}}^{0}\left(1+\frac{x^{2}}{2}+O(x^{4})\right)dx=\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}+\frac{1}{6}n^{-3/2}+O(n^{-5/2})=\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\left(1+O(n^{-1})\right).$$

**Combine.**
$$L_n=\sqrt{n}\cdot\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}}\,\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\left(1+O(n^{-1})\right)\cdot\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\left(1+O(n^{-1})\right)=\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}}\,\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\left(1+O(n^{-1})\right).$$

The powers of $\sqrt{n}$ are $\sqrt{n}\cdot n^{-1/2}\cdot n^{-1/2}=n^{-1/2}$, so the whole expression decays like $n^{-1/2}$ times a constant. Hence
$$L=\lim_{n\to\infty}L_n=\lim_{n\to\infty}\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}}\,\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\left(1+O(n^{-1})\right)=0.$$

**Conclusion.**
$$\boxed{\,L=0\,}$$
